q: Do Silesian steelworks pay CBAM on imported coke and coal?
title: Imported coke and coal under CBAM
short: No. Coal under CN 2701 and coke under 2704 are not in Annex I of the CBAM Regulation, so importing them carries no CBAM obligation. The steelworks pays for burning them through the EU ETS. CBAM applies only if the works imports covered goods such as pig iron, DRI or semi-finished steel.
audience: Steelworks, coke plants and traders in Silesia and other EU coal and steel regions

ul: 2601 11: non-agglomerated iron ore, such as fines and lump.
2601 12 00: agglomerated iron ore, such as pellets and sinter.
7201 and 7203: pig iron, DRI and HBI.

sections.h: Why coke is treated this way
p: CBAM covers goods at the highest risk of carbon leakage from the sectors listed in Annex I. Coke is an input to steel, and its emissions are caught at the EU installation that burns it, under the EU ETS.
